paragraphs: Two kings, one passage, and two very different reports. Jehoshaphat "walked in all the ways of his father Asa" and "did what was right in the eyes of the LORD" (1 Kings 22:43). Ahaziah "did evil in the sight of the LORD and walked in the ways of his father and mother" (1 Kings 22:52). Both of them followed somebody, friend, so the big question is WHO you follow.

Now look at the good king, because the Bible doesn't hide the crumbs. "The high places, however, were not removed" (1 Kings 22:43). Jehoshaphat banished the male shrine prostitutes left from Asa's days (1 Kings 22:46), and he still left some work undone. I think that's honest and kind at the same time: God's Word says plainly what a faithful person got right and what he left standing. Walking with the LORD is not about a spotless kitchen. It is about keeping your feet on His path and keeping at it.

Then there's Ahaziah, who asked to sail with Jehoshaphat's servants and got a no (1 Kings 22:49). The passage doesn't tell us why, so I won't guess. But it does show us that the ways of our fathers and mothers can be a road toward the LORD or away from Him. So here's my question for you, friend: whose footprints are you stepping in today? Pick the ones that lead to Him, and keep walking.
